body.en: Factoring rewrites a polynomial as a product of simpler factors — the key step in solving equations, finding roots, and simplifying rational expressions.

Always take out the greatest common factor (GCF) first. Difference of squares: \( a^{2}-b^{2}=(a-b)(a+b) \). Monic trinomial: \( x^{2}+(p+q)x+pq=(x+p)(x+q) \). For \( ax^2 + bx + c \), use the \( ac \)-method.

Structural Decomposition Theorem: Any proper rational expression \(\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) with \(\deg P < \deg Q\) over \(\mathbb{R}\) decomposes uniquely into a sum of simpler fractions determined by the factorization of \(Q(x)\). When \(\deg P \ge \deg Q\), Euclidean polynomial division yields \(\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)} = Q_{\text{quot}}(x) + \dfrac{R(x)}{Q(x)}\) with \(\deg R < \deg Q\).

For distinct linear factors \((x - a_1)(x - a_2)\), Heaviside's cover-up rule gives the exact residue \(A_k = \lim_{x \to a_k} (x - a_k)\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\). For a repeated factor \((x - a)^m\), all intermediate powers \((x - a)^1, (x - a)^2, \dots, (x - a)^m\) must be included to span the full \(m\)-dimensional rational subspace.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Factoring Polynomials)

body.en:
Why Heaviside Cover-Up & Repeated-Factor Forms Work: Consider \(\dfrac{px + q}{(x - 5)(x + 7)} \equiv \dfrac{A}{x - 5} + \dfrac{B}{x + 7}\). Multiplying both sides by \((x - 5)(x + 7)\) yields the polynomial identity:

\[ px + q \equiv A(x + 7) + B(x - 5) \]

Because two polynomials equal on \(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{5, -7\}\) must be equal for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) by continuity, setting \(x = 5\) annihilates the \(B\) term and isolates \(A = \dfrac{5p + q}{12}\). For a repeated root \((x - a)^2\), writing only \(\dfrac{B}{(x - a)^2}\) restricts the numerator to a constant \(B\), which cannot match a general linear numerator \(px + q\); adding \(\dfrac{A}{x - a}\) supplies \(A(x - a) + B\), spanning all degree-1 numerators.

Factor completely: \( 3x^3 - 75x \).

First extract the greatest common factor (GCF), \( 3x \):

\[ 3x(x^2 - 25). \]

Recognize \( x^2 - 25 \) as a difference of two squares \( a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b) \):

\[ 3x(x - 5)(x + 5). \]

Factor by grouping: \( 2x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x + 15 \).

Group into pairs:

\[ (2x^3 + 6x^2) + (5x + 15). \]

Factor out common terms from each group:

\[ 2x^2(x + 3) + 5(x + 3). \]

Factor out the common binomial factor \( (x + 3) \):

\[ (x + 3)(2x^2 + 5). \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Sum of Squares & Stopping Early

body.en: Two frequent mistakes in factoring: 1. Stopping too early: After factoring out a GCF or one factor, always inspect the remaining polynomial to see if it factors further (e.g. \( x^4 - 16 = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 + 4) = (x - 2)(x + 2)(x^2 + 4) \)). 2. Sum of squares trap: Difference of squares \( a^2 - b^2 \) factors into \( (a - b)(a + b) \), but a sum of squares \( a^2 + b^2 \) is prime over real numbers — it does NOT equal \( (a + b)^2 \)!

Problem (Easy): The radical function \( u(s) = \sqrt{3s + 7} \) is defined for \( 3s + 7 \ge 0 \). Compute the product \( 3s \) when \( u(s) = 8 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Squaring both sides yields \( 3s + 7 = 64 \implies 3s = 57 \).

rows.en: Right-hand side has degree \(-1\) as \(x \to \infty\), whereas LHS approaches \(1\).
Two identical denominators merge into a single fraction, leaving an underdetermined system.
Include every power up to multiplicity: \(\tfrac{A}{x-5} + \tfrac{B}{(x-5)^2}\).
Using \(\tfrac{B}{x^2+7}\) for an irreducible quadratic factor
Fails to account for the \(x\)-term remainder when dividing by a degree-2 factor.
Always use a degree-1 numerator: \(\tfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 7}\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Factoring Polynomials

body.en: 10-Second Sanity Check on Honors Algebra 1 & Foundations: After finding \(A, B, C\), substitute \(x = 0\) (or \(x = 2\)) into both the original rational expression and your partial-fraction sum. If the two numerical fractions do not match, re-check your sign when subtracting negative roots.

solution.en:
Use the \( ac \)-method. We seek two integers whose product is \( a \cdot c = 6(-10) = -60 \) and whose sum is \( b = 11 \).

The factor pair of \( -60 \) that sums to \( 11 \) is \( 15 \) and \( -4 \) (since \( 15 \times (-4) = -60 \) and \( 15 + (-4) = 11 \)).

Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping:

\[ 6x^2 + 15x - 4x - 10 = 3x(2x + 5) - 2(2x + 5). \]

Factor out the binomial \( (2x + 5) \):

\[ (2x + 5)(3x - 2). \]

question.en: Factor the polynomial completely by grouping: \(2x^3 - 3x^2 - 8x + 12\).

solution.en:
Group terms in pairs:

\[(2x^3 - 3x^2) - (8x - 12).\]

Factor out the greatest common factor from each pair:

\[x^2(2x - 3) - 4(2x - 3).\]

Factor out the common binomial \((2x - 3)\):

\[(x^2 - 4)(2x - 3).\]

Recognize \((x^2 - 4)\) as a difference of squares and factor completely:

\[(x - 2)(x + 2)(2x - 3).\]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] The quadratic function \( u(s) = -s^2 + 42s - 210 \) attains its maximum at \( s = v \). Compute the maximum value \( u(v) \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Factoring Polynomials and start from \( u(s) = -s^2 + 42s - 210 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( v = 21 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: The vertex occurs at \( v = 21 \), giving \( u(21) = 441 - 210 = 231 \).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Easy] For all \( s \neq 5 \), the rational expression \( \dfrac{s^2 - 25}{s - 5} \) simplifies to \( s + u \). Compute the scaled constant \( 6u \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Factoring Polynomials and start from \( s \neq 5 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( s + 5 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: Factoring gives \( s + 5 \), so \( u = 5 \) and \( 6u = 30 \).
